[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.

*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:

** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]

* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of [[:en:Fujisawa, Kanagawa|Fujisawa, Kanagawa]], Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** [[:en:Amaterasu|Amaterasu Ōmikami]] (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** [[:en:Ame-no-Tajikarao|Ame-no-Tajikarao]] (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** [[:en:Hachiman|Hachiman]] (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daidō (era)]] 3 ([[:en:808|808]]): A [[:en:Shinto shrine|Shinto shrine]] known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* [[:en:Tenchō|Tenchō (Japanese era)]] 9 ([[:en:832|832]]): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ([[:en:857|857]]): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* [[:en:Tengi|Tenki]] era (1046–1057): [[:en:Minamoto no Yoshiie|Minamoto no Yoshiie]] (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* [[:en:Eiroku|Eiroku (Japanese era)]] era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the [[:en:Shinmei-zukuri|Shinmei-zukuri]] style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** [[:en:Inari shrine|Inari Shrine]]
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: [[:en:Fujisawa Station|JR Fujisawa Station]] or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|WD=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao}} (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|WD=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}} (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daidō (era)}} 3 ({{ill|808|en|808|WD=Q399792|lt=808}}): A {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|WD=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (Japanese era)}} 9 ({{ill|832|en|832|WD=Q23900|lt=832}}): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ({{ill|857|en|857|WD=Q30374|lt=857}}): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|WD=Q1193591|lt=Tenki}} era (1046–1057): {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|WD=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku (Japanese era)}} era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: {{ill|Fujisawa Station|en|Fujisawa Station|WD=Q1133110|lt=JR Fujisawa Station}} or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daidō (era)}} 3 ({{ill|808|en|808|WD=Q399792|lt=808}}): A {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|WD=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (Japanese era)}} 9 ({{ill|832|en|832|WD=Q23900|lt=832}}): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ({{ill|857|en|857|WD=Q30374|lt=857}}): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|WD=Q1193591|lt=Tenki}} era (1046–1057): {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|WD=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku (Japanese era)}} era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}

*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: {{ill|Fujisawa Station|en|Fujisawa Station|WD=Q1133110|lt=JR Fujisawa Station}} or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|WD=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao}} (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|WD=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}} (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daidō (era)}} 3 ({{ill|808|en|808|WD=Q399792|lt=808}}): A {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|WD=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (Japanese era)}} 9 ({{ill|832|en|832|WD=Q23900|lt=832}}): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ({{ill|857|en|857|WD=Q30374|lt=857}}): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|WD=Q1193591|lt=Tenki}} era (1046–1057): {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|WD=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku (Japanese era)}} era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: {{ill|Fujisawa Station|en|Fujisawa Station|WD=Q1133110|lt=JR Fujisawa Station}} or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. == Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|WD=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao}} (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|WD=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}} (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daidō (era)}} 3 ({{ill|808|en|808|WD=Q399792|lt=808}}): A {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|WD=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (Japanese era)}} 9 ({{ill|832|en|832|WD=Q23900|lt=832}}): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ({{ill|857|en|857|WD=Q30374|lt=857}}): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|WD=Q1193591|lt=Tenki}} era (1046–1057): {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|WD=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku (Japanese era)}} era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==

* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).

== Deities ==
* Main enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Amaterasu|en|Amaterasu|WD=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}} (Amaterasu-Ōmikami)
** [[Ame-no-Koyane]] (Amenokoyane-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Tajikarao|en|Ame-no-Tajikarao|WD=Q849412|lt=Ame-no-Tajikarao}} (Amenotajikarao-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Futodama|ja|天太玉命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Futodama|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to フトダマ}} (Amenofutodama-no-Mikoto)
** {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|ja|天宇受売命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to アメノウズメ}} (Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto)
** Ishikoridome-no-Mikoto (石凝刀売命)
* Additional enshrined deities:
** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja|石楯尾大神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Ōkami|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} (Ihatate-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Hachiman|en|Hachiman|WD=Q261637|lt=Hachiman}} (Hachiman-Ōkami)
** {{ill|Kasuga-taisha|ja|春日神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kasuga-taisha|qq=}} (Kasuga-Ōkami)

== History ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Torii.jpg|thumb|250px|First torii, reconstructed in 1960 with reinforced concrete.]]
* {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daidō (era)}} 3 ({{ill|808|en|808|WD=Q399792|lt=808}}): A {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} known as "Ihatate-no-Jinja" was established on the current site of Shinmei-gū.
* {{ill|Tenchō|en|Tenchō|WD=Q1373138|lt=Tenchō (Japanese era)}} 9 ({{ill|832|en|832|WD=Q23900|lt=832}}): The shrine building for Karasumori Shrine (Kōdai-jingū) was constructed on the same grounds as Ihatate Shrine. This is considered the founding year of the shrine.
* {{ill|Ten'an (Japanese era)|ja|天安|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ten'an (Japanese era)|1=Cheonan|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q3577288}} 1 ({{ill|857|en|857|WD=Q30374|lt=857}}): Ihatate Shrine was Ranked as a "Kansha" (officially recognized shrine) at the Rank of "Jūgoi."
* During the reign of Emperor Daigo (醍醐天皇): The shrine was designated as the chief shrine of Tōkami district, known as "Shinmei-gū."
* {{ill|Tengi|en|Tengi|WD=Q1193591|lt=Tenki}} era (1046–1057): {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|en|Minamoto no Yoshiie|WD=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} (Hachiman Tarō Yoshiie) offered prayers at the shrine during his campaign to subdue the Ōshū region.
* {{ill|Eikyū (Heian period)|ja|永久|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eikyū (Heian period)|1=Eikyū (Japan)|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q16277931}} 5 (1117): The shrine was designated as the chief guardian shrine of the Ōba Manor (大庭御厨) area and renamed "Kōdai-jingū."
* {{ill|Eiroku|en|Eiroku|WD=Q1143341|lt=Eiroku (Japanese era)}} era: The shrine continued to serve as a key religious site for the area, undergoing multiple reconstructions and expansions.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}
*** {{ill|Akiba Shrine|ja|秋葉神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Akiba Shrine|qq=}}
*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: {{ill|Fujisawa Station|en|Fujisawa Station|WD=Q1133110|lt=JR Fujisawa Station}} or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

== Buildings and Grounds ==
[[File:Kugenuma Kōdai-jingū -Ise-no-miya.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Ise-no-Miya Shrine within the grounds.</center>]]
The shrine grounds cover an area of 3,300 tsubo and feature old-growth trees, including hundreds-of-years-old tabunoki (machilus) and zelkova, forming a sacred forest. The shrine's name "Karasumori" (Crow Forest) originates from the large number of crows inhabiting the area.
* Main shrine: Constructed in the {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|en|Shinmei-zukuri|WD=Q930545|lt=Shinmei-zukuri|1=Shinmei-zukuri}} style, the current structure was rebuilt in 1984 after nearly 400 years.
* Subsidiary shrines:
*** {{ill|Ontake Shrine|ja|御嶽神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ontake Shrine|1=Mitake shrine|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11488964}}

*** {{ill|Ihatate-no-Jinja|ja|石楯尾神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ihatate-no-Jinja|qq=}}
*** Ise-no-Miya
*** {{ill|Inari shrine|en|Inari shrine|WD=Q514480|lt=Inari Shrine|1=Inari shrine}}
*** Other small shrines dedicated to regional and national deities.
* Festival floats storage: Dedicated spaces for 9 traditional floats used during the shrine's annual festival.

== Festivals and Annual Events ==
[[File:勢揃い１.jpg|thumb|250px|<center>Festival floats at the annual festival.</center>]]
* New Year’s Festival (January 1)
* festival (August 17)
*** Known as one of the major festivals in Kanagawa Prefecture, featuring 9 ornate floats and traditional performances.
* Monthly offerings (1st and 15th of each month)
* Seasonal rites, including rituals for good harvest, protection from insects, and exorcisms.

== Access ==
The shrine is located at 2-11-5 Kugenuma Shinmei, Fujisawa, Kanagawa.
* Nearest stations: {{ill|Fujisawa Station|en|Fujisawa Station|WD=Q1133110|lt=JR Fujisawa Station|1=Fujisawa Station}} or nearby bus stops.
* Parking available.

[[Kōdai-jingū]] is a regional [[Sōja shrine|Sōja shrine]]. It enshrines many kami of the local region.

It contrasts with provincial Soja shrines which enshrine all the kami of a province<ref>https://archive.ph/wip/XtZfZ</ref>

{{統合文字|鵠}}

'''Kōdai-jingū''' (皇大神宮) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|WD=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in the {{ill|Kugenuma|ja|鵠沼|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kugenuma|1=Kugenuma|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11675779}} district of {{ill|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|en|Fujisawa, Kanagawa|WD=Q386661|lt=Fujisawa, Kanagawa|1=Fujisawa, Kanagawa}}, Japan. The official name of the shrine is "Kōdai-jingū," but it is also referred to as "Shinmei-gū" or "Karasumori Shrine." It is classified as a {{ill|village shrine|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}} under the old shrine Ranking system. The shrine serves as the chief guardian deity of the former Tōkami district (土甘郷, later Kugenuma Village) and is affectionately known as "Shinmei-sama" (神明様).
